the requirement that owns the item. The index names its public fields, methods,
and associated types. The linked requirement gives their signatures and bounds,
enum variants, and explicit trait implementations with their associated types.
Changes to those interfaces require a change to the owning requirement.

Trait methods are listed on their trait. Signatures use Rustdoc’s short type
names. Rustdoc’s automatic and blanket implementations are outside the inventory.

The `trust-but-verify` crate defines no Cargo features. Habeas uses only the
documented TBV public API.

rationale:
**Confirmation:** the assessments disagreed

First assessment `true`: `public_exports_match_the_appendix` in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs` covers every obligation in `requirements.sdk.public-api.exports` and carries the `{test}` marker. Its helpers are reached from that test, so they need no markers of their own. I read the implementation of the test and its helpers. I did not request any implementation source.

Obligation-to-test mapping:
- **Inventory matches the exported items.** `specified_exports` parses the requirement text itself, because `INVENTORY` is `include_str!` of `md/requirements/sdk/public-api.md`. It enforces a crate root, module-only nesting and no duplicates. `documented_exports` walks the freshly generated rustdoc HTML (`cargo doc --no-deps -p trust-but-verify`) from the crate index through every module table. It records the path and kind of each item, panics on unrecognised categories, and panics with "Missing inventory declaration" for an undocumented-in-inventory item. The final `assert!` compares `specified.difference(&documented)` and `documented.difference(&specified)` in both directions, so both a missing export and an unlisted one fail the test.
- **Each declaration link opens the owning requirement.** `declaration_target` requires an anchor and derives the namespace from the chapter path. The anchor must be `habeas-req-<namespace>.<name>`, and declarations may not point to `public-api.md`. `check_declaration` then reads the chapter and requires the `:::{req} <name>` block, a description line and a ```` ```rust,ignore ```` declaration. Linked method and associated-type declarations are checked the same way.
- **The index names public fields, methods and associated types.** `check_declaration` asserts `link.members == rustdoc.member_names(page)`. That helper collects rustdoc's fields, implementations, required and provided methods, associated types and associated consts.
- **The linked requirement gives signatures, bounds, variants and explicit trait impls with associated types.** `check_declaration` compares `signature_parts(declaration)` with the rustdoc item declaration and inherent impl members, keyed by impl bounds, and reports both missing and unexpected parts. It also compares `expected_impls` with `rustdoc.trait_impls(page)`, which includes associated types and consts. Enum variants are part of the rustdoc item declaration. It also requires `#[non_exhaustive]` on structs with public fields.
- **Changes to interfaces require a change to the owning requirement.** Any drift between the Rust API and the requirement text fails the comparisons above. `member_order_is_free_but_field_and_method_types_are_committed` checks that `signature_parts` ignores member order but rejects changed field types, return types and receivers.
- **Trait methods are listed on their trait.** `member_names` runs on trait pages for required and provided methods.
- **Rustdoc's automatic and blanket implementations are outside the inventory.** `trait_impls` reads only the `trait-implementations` and `foreign-impls` sections, and skips the `StructuralPartialEq` marker. Automatic and blanket impls live in separate sections that it never reads.
- **No Cargo features.** The test asserts that `sdk["features"] == {}` in `cargo metadata`.
- **Habeas uses only the documented TBV public API.** The test runs `cargo check --package habeas --lib`, which must succeed. Habeas can only use public items, and the inventory check shows that every public item is documented.

Each public SDK item has one defining module path. The SDK exposes no public
re-exports. The chapter that introduces each supported type or free function owns its declaration.
The [public API inventory](sdk/public-api.md) links each item to that requirement,
and declares its public Rust interface, including fields, enum variants, trait
members, and inherent methods. A change to that interface requires a change to
the owning requirement. Every supported struct with public fields is
`#[non_exhaustive]`. Its constructor accepts the values needed to create it.
Additional fields have consuming builder methods that accept a concrete value.
Optional fields start as `None`. Backend inference options start empty and can
be added one key at a time.
The SDK’s public modules follow the interfaces introduced in these chapters.
- `domain`: application data and the `Domain` and `NodeContents` traits.
- `graph`: criterion definitions, graph observations, evidence, and functions for running criteria.
- `request`: `ValidationContext`, typed `Ask` builders, context values, and request phases.
- `sources`: project inspection, search queries, and their results.
- `outline`: selectable source contents and language rules; `outline::languages`
supplies bundled languages, and `outline::selector` defines selector syntax.
Source access, search engines, redaction, provider transports, agent-result paging,
and conversation machinery are implementation details of those interfaces.
